stories.title: The Joyita: Found Adrift With No One Aboard
stories.hook: 25 people sailed. The ship came back without them.
stories.summary: In 1955 the Joyita left Samoa on a two-day voyage. Thirty-seven days later she was found drifting near Fiji, still afloat - and every one of the 25 people aboard was gone.

image.alt: AI reconstruction: a small ship drifting alone on a grey Pacific sea

sources.label: NZ Herald - Author says he's solved MV Joyita mystery
RNZ - Call for coronial hearing into Tokelau's Joyita tragedy

stories.title: Judar Pasha: The Slave Boy Who Marched Across the Sahara
stories.hook: Born in Spain. Enslaved as a boy. Then he led an army across the Sahara.
stories.summary: In 1590 a Moroccan sultan sent thousands of men and animals across the world's largest hot desert to attack the Songhai Empire. The man he chose to lead them was a eunuch born in Spain.

image.alt: AI reconstruction: an army column with camels crossing Saharan dunes

sources.label: Legado Andalusí - The African deed of Judar Pasha
Warfare History Network - Africa: The Ultimate Frontier II

stories.title: George Psalmanazar: The Man From Nowhere
stories.hook: He told London he came from a faraway island. For years, people believed him.
stories.summary: In the early 1700s a Frenchman claimed to be the first native of Formosa - today's Taiwan - ever to visit Europe. Many in Britain believed him, until he was revealed to be European.

image.alt: AI reconstruction: a crowded 1700s London street at dusk

stories.title: The Owlers: England's Night-Time Wool Smugglers
stories.hook: For 450 years, smuggling wool out of England was a crime. The smugglers worked at night.
stories.summary: Taking sheep or wool from England to another country - especially France - was illegal from 1367 until 1824. The smugglers were called owlers, and their boats owling boats.

image.alt: AI reconstruction: smugglers loading wool bales onto a boat at night

stories.title: Kakongo: The Kingdom on the Atlantic Coast
stories.hook: A small kingdom of Central Africa that became a major trading power.
stories.summary: Kakongo stood on the Atlantic coast of Central Africa, in today's Republic of the Congo and Cabinda, Angola. With its neighbours Loango and Ngoyo it became an important political and commercial centre from the 17th to the 19th century.

image.alt: AI reconstruction: a trading settlement on the Central African Atlantic coast
